title: A instancias de: señalar quién impulsó una acción

sections.content: A instancias de (at the urging of, at the instigation of) names the specific person or group who pushed for an action to happen -- useful in historical writing when it matters who was really behind a decision, not just that it happened. It's followed by a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: A instancias del presidente Reagan, Estados Unidos comenzó a financiar, entrenar y armar a los Contras desde bases en Honduras.
items.english: At President Reagan's urging, the United States began financing, training, and arming the Contras from bases in Honduras.

items.spanish: A instancias de algunos miembros del propio gobierno, se buscaron formas alternativas de seguir financiando a los Contras.
items.english: At the urging of some members of the government itself, alternative ways of continuing to fund the Contras were sought.

items.spanish: Cuba y la Unión Soviética proporcionaron apoyo militar a instancias de sus propios intereses geopolíticos.
items.english: Cuba and the Soviet Union provided military support at the instigation of their own geopolitical interests.

items.spanish: A instancias del Congreso, se aprobó una ley que limitaba considerablemente la ayuda oficial a esta guerra encubierta.
items.english: At Congress's urging, a law was passed that considerably limited official aid to this covert war.

sections.content: A instancias de is more specific than por -- it points to whoever actively pushed for or requested the action, which makes it useful for tracing responsibility in a historical narrative.
